Mod.Name: Memoria Dev Console
Mod.Author: Robert McFarlane
Mod.Description:
MEMORIA DEV CONSOLE ===================
A development and testing utility for FINAL FANTASY IX modding with Memoria.
Memoria Dev Console adds a detached, second-monitor-friendly development console that runs alongside the game and puts common modding, testing, logging, compilation, restart, field-save-state, and model-viewing tools in one place.
The goal is simple: spend less time closing the game, digging through files, relaunching tools, and rebuilding test states — and more time actually developing and testing your mod.
DEV CONSOLE FEATURES --------------------
LIVE LOG • Displays Memoria.log in a dedicated live console view. • Automatically follows new log entries as they are written. • The game remains fully playable while the Live Log is open. • Useful for watching script output, errors, warnings, battle behavior, field events, and other runtime information on a second monitor while testing.
COMPILE + RESTART • Runs the standard Memoria.Compiler against the installed Memoria script sources. • Displays compiler output directly in the Dev Console. • After compilation, FINAL FANTASY IX is hard restarted so newly compiled script DLLs can be loaded by the new process. • Designed for rapid edit → compile → test iteration when developing C# script mods. • Normal C# compile errors are now reported as compile failures without breaking the Dev Console; restart is simply aborted until the source is fixed.
MODEL VIEWER • Opens Memoria's Model Viewer directly from the running game without requiring a trip through the launcher. • Intended for quickly checking model IDs, animations, weapons, geometry, and other model information during development. • Existing field UI and field rendering are isolated while the viewer is active. • When the Model Viewer closes, the Dev Console rolls the game back to the most recent stable field state so testing can continue cleanly.
HARD RESET • Hard restarts FINAL FANTASY IX without returning to the Memoria launcher. • Useful when editing data such as BattlePatch.txt, DictionaryPatch.txt, or other parameters that require a fresh game process before changes can be tested. • Provides a much faster edit → reset → test loop than manually closing and relaunching the game.
FIELD SAVE STATES • Maintains a rolling timeline of recent stable field save states while you play. • Move backward and forward through captured field save states for rapid testing. • Set a separate checkpoint and return to it when repeatedly testing the same sequence, cutscene, trigger, NPC, boss encounter, or field script. • Field history can be preserved across Dev Console hard restarts, making repeated testing much faster than loading saves and replaying the same route.
ASSET DUMPER • Runs complete-game development dumps directly from the Dev Console. • Field Background Dump reconstructs every internal field into per-field BGX metadata and editable PNG overlays under FieldDumper_Output in the game root. • 2D Texture Dump loads every known GEO model and exports its runtime model textures as PNGs under 2D Texture Dump Output in the game root. • These are intentionally whole-game dumps and create a large number of files. • The integrated texture dump does not dump animations.
RESET TO LAUNCHER • Shuts FINAL FANTASY IX down and restarts the Memoria launcher instead of immediately relaunching the game. • Use this when you need to enable or disable mods, change mod priority/order, alter launcher options, or adjust Memoria settings before the next test.
CONTROLLER + KEYBOARD WORKFLOW • The Dev Console supports keyboard and controller navigation. • F10 globally shows or hides the console. • Controller Hotkey: Press R2 + R1 + L2 + L1 + D-Pad Down to open or close the Memoria Dev Console. • Controller shortcuts are available for fast console access and hard resets during testing. • The console freezes normal game processing on development pages where isolation is required, while Live Log remains passive so the game can be played normally while logs are monitored.
The Dev Console is intended as a development utility rather than a gameplay mod. It is especially useful for field scripting, battle scripting, custom C# development, model/animation work, patch-file editing, compatibility testing, and repeated encounter testing.
HWS CUSTOM ID INPUT SAVER — OPTIONAL SEPARATE TOOL ===================================================
The HWS Custom ID Input Saver is a small companion tool I made to speed up working with custom fields and custom battles in Hades Workshop.
WHAT IT DOES ------------
When exporting a custom field or custom battle in Hades Workshop, the export dialog contains several dropdowns and ID inputs that need to be filled out.
When you're repeatedly editing and re-exporting the same custom content, filling out those same values over and over gets tedious.
The HWS Custom ID Input Saver remembers the values entered in those Hades Workshop export dialogs and automatically restores them the next time the dialog is opened.
This lets you:
• Set up your custom field or custom battle export once. • Close the export dialog and continue editing in Hades Workshop. • Reopen the export dialog later with your previous dropdown selections and ID inputs already restored. • Re-export and iterate without repeatedly filling out the same custom ID information.
WHY IT IS NOT INCLUDED ----------------------
The HWS Custom ID Input Saver is a separate Windows EXE and is not included with this Nexus download because the executable will not pass Nexus Mods' virus scan.
Rather than include an EXE that causes the mod archive to be flagged, I have left it out of the public download.
If you're interested in using the HWS Custom ID Input Saver, private message me.
